title: Terraforming Mars
scope: Setup, then generations of actions and production until temperature, oxygen and oceans all reach their goals; 2–5 players on one phone; optional Prelude, Venus Next, Colonies, Turmoil and the Hellas & Elysium maps

victory.note: When temperature, oxygen and oceans are all at their goals, the game ends after that generation’s production: everyone may turn plants into greenery once more (in player order), then score TR, awards, milestones, greeneries and cities, and cards. Most VP wins; ties go to the most M€.

citations.excerpt: When all three global parameters (ocean, temperature, and oxygen) have reached their goals, the game ends at the end of that generation.
players have one extra chance to convert plants into greenery tiles (in player order
Gives the leading player in that category 5 VPs and the runner-up 2 VPs (except in a 2-player game).
Each claimed Milestone is worth 5 VPs.
Each greenery tile is worth 1 VP and each city tile is worth 1 VP for each greenery adjacent to it
The player with the highest total score is the winner! Any ties are won by having the most M€.

expansions.title: Prelude
expansions.summary: Prelude cards at setup for a faster start, plus 7 project cards and 5 corporations.

expansions.title: Venus Next
expansions.summary: The Venus board and scale, Air Scrapping, floaters, and World Government terraforming each generation.

expansions.title: Colonies
expansions.summary: Colony tiles and trade fleets: build colonies and trade with them.

expansions.title: Turmoil
expansions.summary: The Terraforming Committee: delegates, ruling parties, Global Events and a TR revision each generation.

expansions.title: Hellas or Elysium map

steps.title: Board
steps.instruction: Place the game board in the middle of the table, then:
bullets: Put the 9 ocean tiles on their reserved space.
Temperature and oxygen markers on their starting spaces; the generation marker on 1 on the TR track.
Resource cubes and the other tiles within everyone’s reach.

citations.excerpt: Place the 9 ocean tiles on their reserved space.
Place the temperature and oxygen markers on their starting positions.
Also place the generation marker on ’1’ on the TR track.
Resource cubes and remaining tiles are placed so that everyone can reach them.

additions.text: Playing on Hellas or Elysium? Use that board instead of Tharsis. It has its own placement bonuses, ocean areas, milestones and awards:
bullets: Hellas: the south pole costs 6 M€ to place a tile on, and gives you an ocean tile (with its TR) to place on any ocean area.
Hellas has no volcanos or Noctis region: Noctis City and Lava Flows tiles may go on any non-ocean area.
Elysium has no Noctis region either, so Noctis City has no restriction. Lava Flows may go on Arsia Mons, Olympus Mons, Elysium Mons or Hecates Tholus.

citations.excerpt: Any of these two game boards can be used instead of the ordinary game board.
requiring you to pay 6 megacredits for placing a tile here, but giving you an ocean tile
so the tiles from the cards Noctis City and Lava Flows lose their placement restrictions and may be placed on any non-ocean area.
four volcanic sites where the Lava Flows tile can be placed: Arsia Mons, Olympus Mons, Elysium Mons, and Hecates Tholus.

additions.text: Place the Venus board next to the game board:
bullets: White marker on 0% of the Venus scale.
Hoverlord milestone tile over the Milestones headline, Venuphile award tile over the Awards headline: 3 of 6 can now be claimed or funded.

citations.excerpt: During setup, the Venus board is placed next to the game board, with a white marker on 0%, at the start of the Venus scale.
so that 3 out of 6 Milestones may be claimed.
Place this tile so that it covers the Awards headline on the game board.

additions.text: Place the Trade Fleets tile next to the game board, then:
bullets: Draw colony tiles: the number of players plus 2 (5 with 2 players).
Put a white cube on the highlighted second step of each colony track.
Titan, Enceladus and Miranda: the cube starts on the moon picture, and moves to the second step once any card in play can collect their resource. No colonies or trade there until then.

citations.excerpt: Place the Trade Fleets Tile next to the game board.
draw tiles equal to the number of players plus 2
use 5 tiles if playing a 2 player game.
Place a white cube on the highlighted second step of each Colony Tile track.
TITAN, ENCELADUS, and MIRANDA start with their white marker on the moon picture itself

additions.text: Place the Terraforming Committee board and the Global Event board next to the game board:
bullets: On Tharsis, cover the Terraformer milestone with the new tile (TR 26).
A gray neutral delegate in the Chairman seat; the other neutral delegates in the Neutral Reserve.

Shuffle the Global Event cards onto their space. Draw one as the Coming Global Event and put a neutral delegate as Party Leader of the party at its top left: that party is Dominant (Dominance marker in its delegate area).
Turn the next card face up as the Distant Global Event and add a neutral delegate to its top-left party (in the delegate area if that party already has a leader).
Stack the six Policy tiles with Greens on top: Greens rule the first generation, which has no Current Global Event.

citations.excerpt: Place the Terraforming Committee board and Global Event board next to the main game board.
replace the Terraformer milestone with the new tile, requiring only TR 26.
Place a gray neutral delegate in the Chairman seat
Shuffle the Global Event cards and place the deck on the reserved space on the Global Event board.
Place a neutral delegate as Party Leader in the party indicated at the top left of the card.
If it is in the same party as the other neutral delegate, place it in the area for delegates instead.
Place all six Policy tiles in a pile at their designated place on the Terraforming Committee board, with GREENS on top.
There is no CURRENT Global Event to execute the first generation.

steps.title: Decks
bullets: Standard game: take every Corporate Era card (red and white icon, lower left) out of the project cards and the corporations.
Shuffle the project deck and put it next to the board, with room for a discard pile.

citations.excerpt: Make sure you have no Corporate Era cards in the project deck or among the corporation cards.
Shuffle the project cards and place the project deck next to the board.

additions.title: Corporate Era
additions.text: Playing the extended game? Keep every Corporate Era card, including its 2 corporations. Players then start without the extra production.

citations.excerpt: To play the extended game, simply add all cards marked with a red and white icon
Players start with no extra production of resources

additions.text: Shuffle Prelude’s 7 project cards into the project deck and its 5 corporations into the corporations. Shuffle the other 35 cards, the Prelude cards, into a deck of their own.

citations.excerpt: you shuffle the 7 project cards into the main project card deck, and the 5 corporations into the corporation deck.
The remaining 35 cards are referred to as Prelude cards, and are shuffled into a deck of their own.

additions.text: Shuffle the 49 Venus project cards and 5 Venus corporations into their decks.

citations.excerpt: The various projects in this expansion are represented by 49 new project cards, as well as 5 new corporations to choose from.
Shuffle these into the respective decks before dealing cards and corporations

additions.text: Shuffle the Colonies project cards and corporations into their decks.

citations.excerpt: Shuffle the project cards together with the main game project cards, and the Colony corporation cards together with the other corporation cards.

additions.text: Shuffle the 16 Turmoil project cards into the project deck.

citations.excerpt: Shuffle the 16 new Turmoil project cards into the main project card deck.

steps.title: Players
steps.instruction: Choose who goes first, then each player:
bullets: The player who most recently won Terraforming Mars takes the first player marker.
Choose a color; take its player markers and a player board.
Standard game: 1 production of every resource (a marker on 1 on all six tracks).
One marker on 20 on the TR track.

citations.excerpt: The player who most recently won a game of Terraforming Mars is given the first player marker.
Players choose their colors and take the corresponding player markers and a player board.
You start with 1 production of each resource on the player board
Each player also places one marker at the starting position (20) of the TR track.

additions.text: Each player puts a trade fleet on the Trade Fleets tile, with a player marker inside it.

citations.excerpt: and place it on the Trade Fleets Tile, with your player marker inside it

additions.text: Each player puts 1 of their 7 delegates in the Lobby and the other 6 in the Delegate Reserve.

citations.excerpt: Each player takes their seven delegate markers and places one in the Lobby of the Terraforming Committee board and the other six in the Delegate Reserve.

steps.title: Deal cards
bullets: New players: a Beginner Corporation, which gives 42 M€ and 10 project cards straight to their hand. They skip the rest of setup’s choices.
Everyone else: 2 corporations (without the Corporate Era ones in a standard game) and 10 project cards.

citations.excerpt: Players new to Terraforming Mars each get a Beginner Corporation card
to get 42 MegaCredits and draw 10 project cards to form their starting hand.
Shuffle the 10 standard corporation cards (excluding the 2 Corporate Era corporations) and deal 2 to each remaining player.
Deal 10 cards to each remaining player.

additions.text: Also deal 4 Prelude cards to each player.

citations.excerpt: you also deal 4 Prelude cards to each player.

steps.title: Choose and reveal
steps.instruction: Everyone chooses at once, then reveals in player order:
bullets: Pick 1 corporation and which of the 10 project cards to keep.
Discard the rest face down (corporations go back in the box).
In player order: reveal your corporation, take its starting resources and production, then pay 3 M€ for each card you keep.

citations.excerpt: Players choose which of the corporations they want to play, and which of the 10 project cards they want to keep for their starting hand.
cards are always discarded face down!
In player order, players then reveal their chosen corporation, get their starting resources and production (if any), and then pay 3 M€ for each project card they keep.

additions.text: Also keep 2 of your 4 Prelude cards, for free. Once everyone has paid, play your 2 Preludes in player order and discard the other 2. They work like green cards.

citations.excerpt: The players choose 2 Prelude cards to keep at the same time as choosing corporations and project cards
The Prelude cards do not cost anything to keep.
each player plays their pair of picked Prelude cards in player order, and discards their remaining 2 Prelude cards.
They work like green cards, and stay in play with their tags visible.

steps.title: Generation 1
steps.instruction: Generation 1 has no Player Order or Research phase: the first player starts the action phase.

citations.excerpt: The first generation starts without a player order phase and without a research phase
so the first player just starts the action phase.

loop.note: Clockwise from the first player. Take 1 or 2 actions, or pass: once you pass, you’re out until the next generation.

citations.excerpt: Play proceeds clockwise around the table until all players have passed.
If you take no action at all (pass), you are out of the round and may not take any anymore actions this generation.

steps.title: 1 or 2 actions
steps.instruction: Take 1 or 2 actions, in any combination, or pass:
bullets: Play a card: meet its requirement and pay its cost (steel is worth 2 M€ on building tags, titanium 3 M€ on space tags), then do its effects.
Standard project: Sell patents (discard cards for 1 M€ each), Power plant 11 M€, Asteroid 14 M€, Aquifer 18 M€, Greenery 23 M€, City 25 M€.
Claim a milestone you qualify for: 8 M€, worth 5 VP. Only 3 can be claimed.
Fund an award: 8, then 14, then 20 M€. Only 3 can be funded.
Use the action on a blue card, once a generation.
Turn 8 plants into a greenery tile (raises oxygen), or 8 heat into a temperature step.

citations.excerpt: Players take 1 or 2 actions each turn, or pass.
In order to play a card you must meet its requirements and be able to perform the effects
Steel: Is only used to pay for cards with a building tag and is worth 2 M€/cube.
Titanium: Is only used to pay for cards with a space tag and is worth 3 M€/cube
Sell patents: You may discard a number of cards from hand to gain the same number of M€.
Power plant: For 11 M€ you get to increase your energy production 1 step.
Asteroid: For 14 M€ you get to increase temperature 1 step
Aquifer: For 18 M€ you get to place an ocean tile
Greenery: For 23 M€ you get to place a greenery tile
City: For 25 M€ you get to place a city tile
only 3 of the 5 milestones may be claimed in total
Each claimed milestone is worth 5 VPs at the end of the game.
The first player to fund an award pays 8 M€ and places a player marker on it.
The next player to fund an award pays 14 M€, the last pays 20 M€.
Each such action card may be used once each generation.
8 plant resources may be turned into a greenery tile
8 heat resources may be spent to increase temperature 1 step

additions.title: Placing tiles
bullets: Take the bonus printed on its area, plus 2 M€ for each ocean next to it.
Oceans only on ocean areas; never a city next to another city; a greenery next to one of your tiles if you can.
Raising temperature, oxygen or oceans raises your TR too, except once that parameter has reached its goal.

citations.excerpt: When you place the tile, you receive the placement bonus printed on that area (if any).
Each ocean tile on the board provides a 2 M€ placement bonus for any player later placing a tile
Ocean tiles may only be placed on areas reserved for ocean
May not be placed next to another city
If possible, greenery tiles must be placed next to another tile that you own.
Whenever you raise one of them, your terraform rating also increases by that much
When a global parameter has reached its goal, it can’t be raised any further, and so does not increase your TR.

bullets: Air Scrapping (standard project): 15 M€ to raise Venus 1 step, and your TR.
Venus bonuses: draw a card at 8%, an extra TR at 16%.
Hoverlord milestone: 7 floaters on your cards. Venuphile award: most Venus tags.

citations.excerpt: A new standard project, Air Scrapping, allows players to increase the Venus scale one step for 15 M€, gaining a TR as normal.
When increasing Venus to 8%, you get to draw a card for free.
When increasing Venus to 16%, you get an extra TR.
To claim Hoverlord, you need a total of at least 7 floater resources on your cards.
Venuphile Award is a contest for most Venus tags in play.

bullets: Build a colony (standard project, 17 M€): your marker on the lowest free spot of a colony track; take its placement bonus. At most 3 colonies per tile, and 1 of yours.

Trade: pay 9 M€, 3 energy or 3 titanium and move your trade fleet onto a colony tile with no fleet. Take the trade income at the white marker; colony owners there get their colony bonus. Then slide the white marker left, next to the colonies.

citations.excerpt: This is a standard project that costs 17 M€
Only 3 colonies total per Colony Tile are allowed
Each player may only have one colony per Colony Tile
Pay the cost: 9 M€, or 3 energy, or 3 titanium
A Colony Tile may only hold 1 trade fleet at a time.
Directly after trading you move the white marker as far left as possible, stopping next to the player colonies

bullets: Lobbying, any number of times: move a delegate from the Lobby (free) or your Delegate Reserve (5 M€) into a party.
More delegates in a party than its leader makes you Party Leader; the party with the most delegates is Dominant.
The ruling party’s policy works during the action phase.
A card with a party requirement needs that party ruling, or 2 of your delegates in it.

citations.excerpt: Move one of your delegates from the Delegate Reserve (costs 5 M€), or from the Lobby (for free!), into the Delegate Area of your desired party
they replace the Party Leader marker with one of their own from that party.
The party with the most delegates is the Dominant party
The effect or action on the Policy tile is active only during the Action phase.
that card is playable only if that party is currently ruling
OR if you have at least 2 delegates in that party.

reminders.text: Used a blue card’s action? Leave a player marker on it.

citations.excerpt: place a player marker on the card to indicate that it has been used this generation.

reminders.text: Raised a parameter? Move your TR up too, and take any bonus printed on that step of the track.

citations.excerpt: Whenever you raise one of them, your terraform rating also increases by that much
If you raise the parameter to this point, you also get the attached bonus.

reminders.text: Took no action? Then you’ve passed: you’re out until the next generation.

citations.excerpt: If you take no action at all (pass), you are out of the round and may not take any anymore actions this generation.

reminders.text: Traded? Your fleet stays on that colony tile until the end of the generation.

citations.excerpt: When the generation ends, all trade fleets move back from the Colony Tiles to the Trade Fleets Tile

steps.title: Production
bullets: Turn all energy into heat (move the cubes to the heat box).
Gain M€ equal to your TR plus your M€ production (which may be negative).
Gain every other resource you produce.
Take the player markers off used action cards.

citations.excerpt: First, all energy is converted into heat
Players get M€ according to their terraform rating plus any M€ production (which may be negative!)
then the players also get any other resources they have production of according to the player board.
Finally, remove player markers from used action cards

steps.title: Is Mars terraformed?
steps.instruction: Are temperature (+8 °C), oxygen (14%) and all 9 oceans at their goals?
bullets: Yes: the game ends. In player order, everyone may turn plants into greenery tiles once more, then score. End the game from the Game menu.
No: carry on with the generation.

citations.excerpt: When all three global parameters (ocean, temperature, and oxygen) have reached their goals, the game ends at the end of that generation.
players have one extra chance to convert plants into greenery tiles (in player order
The game ends when there is enough oxygen to breathe (14 %), oceans enough to allow Earth-like weather (9), and the temperature is well above freezing (+8

additions.text: The Venus scale doesn’t need to be finished for the game to end.

citations.excerpt: But the Venus scale is not an end game condition

additions.text: If the game ends, skip Turmoil. In the final scoring, each Party Leader and the Chairman is worth 1 VP to its owner.

citations.excerpt: When the game ends, the Turmoil step is not performed.
all Party Leaders and the Chairman are worth 1 VP for the respective player.

steps.title: World Government terraforming
steps.instruction: The first player (the order hasn’t shifted yet) raises one global parameter that isn’t at its goal by 1 step, or places an ocean tile, for the World Government:
bullets: No TR or bonuses for the first player.
Cards may still trigger, such as Arctic Algae or Aphrodite.

citations.excerpt: The first player (player order hasn’t yet shifted) now acts as the WG, and chooses a non-maxed global parameter and increases that track one step, or places an ocean tile.
All bonuses go to the WG, and therefore no TR or other bonuses are given to the first player.

steps.title: Colony production
bullets: Return the trade fleets to the Trade Fleets tile.
Move the white marker 1 step up the colony track.

citations.excerpt: Return all Trade Fleets from the Colony Tiles to the Trade Fleets Tile.
Move the white marker one step up the Colony track on each Colony Tile.

steps.title: TR revision and Global Event
bullets: Everyone loses 1 TR.

Resolve the Current Global Event (there’s none in generation 1). Anything it counts stops at 5, then add each player’s influence: 1 each for the Chairman, the leader of the Dominant party, and other delegates in the Dominant party.

citations.excerpt: after the Production phase, ALL players lose 1 TR
Perform the Current Global Event, taking influence into account
can only count up to a maximum of 5
Owning the Chairman gives 1 influence.
Owning the leader of the Dominant party gives 1 influence.
Owning 1 or more non-leader delegates in the Dominant party gives 1 influence.

steps.title: New Government
bullets: Its Policy tile goes on top: it rules the next generation.
Everyone gets its Ruling Bonus.
Return the old Chairman and the party’s other delegates to their reserves.
Its Party Leader becomes Chairman, and that player gains 1 TR.
Move the Dominance marker to the party with the most delegates (ties: the next one clockwise).
Refill the Lobby: 1 delegate per player from their reserve.

citations.excerpt: The Dominant party now becomes ruling. Change Policy tile.
Resolve the Ruling Bonus (affects all players).
Return the former Chairman and all non-leader delegates from Dominant party to reserve.
Party Leader from the Dominant party becomes new Chairman, earning 1 TR.
Dominance marker goes to new Dominant party (or clockwise in case of tie).
Fill the lobby from the reserve so that each player has 1 delegate there.

steps.title: Changing Times
bullets: The Coming Global Event goes onto the Current one; add the neutral delegate shown at its middle right.
The Distant Global Event becomes the Coming one.
Turn the top card face up as the Distant Global Event, add its top-left neutral delegate and read its flavor text.

citations.excerpt: Place the Coming Global Event on top of the Current Global Event.
Add the neutral delegate indicated at the mid-right on that card.
Move the Distant Global Event into the Coming Global Event space.
Turn the top card of the Global Event deck face up, add the top-left neutral delegate, and read the flavor text.

steps.title: Player order
steps.instruction: Pass the first player marker 1 step clockwise and move the generation marker up 1.

citations.excerpt: The first player marker shifts 1 step clockwise and the generation marker is moved up 1 step.

steps.title: Research
steps.instruction: Everyone draws 4 cards and buys the ones they want:
bullets: 3 M€ for each card you keep (0–4).
Discard the rest face down.
There’s no hand limit.

citations.excerpt: Each player draws 4 cards and decides which of them he wants to buy to his hand.
Each card costs 3 M€ to buy to the hand, and you may buy 0-4 cards.
The rest of the 4 drawn cards are discarded face down on the discard pile. There is no hand limit.
